finding.claim: The /checkout endpoint computes the charge from client-supplied price and qty. An attacker can set price to a tiny value, or price or qty to negative values. This undercharges them, or produces a zero or negative total that credits or refunds the account.

trace.note: total = sum of i.price * i.qty taken directly from the request body, with no catalog lookup, type check or range check
total is passed to the payment charge call unchanged
the attacker-chosen total is returned as the charged amount

finding.guards_checked: No server-side price lookup. No validation of qty (negative, fractional, non-numeric) or price. No check that total > 0. No schema validation. The sibling /checkout-v2 route shows the correct pattern, so this route is the unfixed one. Auth middleware is not visible in this file.

verdict.reason: cart.js:5 sums client-supplied i.price * i.qty with no catalog lookup or validation, and cart.js:6 passes it unchanged to req.payments.charge, whereas /checkout-v2 (cart.js:13-14) uses catalog prices and clamps qty. Any authenticated user who can reach the route can exploit this. No auth or validation middleware exists in the only file in the directory, so none could be checked.

verdict_facts.reason: cart.js:5 sums client-supplied i.price * i.qty with no catalog lookup or range check, and cart.js:6-7 pass that total to req.payments.charge and return it, while the sibling /checkout-v2 (cart.js:13-14) shows the missing server-side price lookup and qty clamp. An authenticated user (req.user is set upstream) can therefore set a tiny or negative price or qty.

finding.claim: In /checkout-v2 the qty is not validated as a finite number. A non-numeric qty such as a string or an object makes Math.floor return NaN, and Math.max(1, NaN) is NaN, so total becomes NaN. An extremely large qty makes the total Infinity or overflows it. The unvalidated total is passed to charge(), where a payment backend may treat NaN as 0 or fail open. Items with a missing or unknown sku can also return an undefined price, which also yields NaN.

trace.note: iterates req.body.items with no check that it is an array of well-formed objects
the catalog price may be undefined or NaN for an unknown sku
Math.max(1, Math.floor(NaN)) is NaN, which poisons the running total
the NaN, Infinity or zero total is charged without validation

finding.guards_checked: Math.max(1, ...) blocks negative and zero qty, but not NaN, Infinity or huge values. There is no Number.isFinite or Number.isSafeInteger check, no cap on qty, and no check that total is finite and > 0. Whether charge() rejects NaN is not visible in this file, so impact depends on the payments implementation.

verdict.guard_found: none in cart.js; the only visible clamp is Math.max(1, Math.floor(i.qty)) at cart.js:14, which does not stop NaN. charge() and catalog.price() are injected on req and not defined in the available code.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (cart.js:12-16: a non-numeric qty or an unknown sku gives NaN at line 14, which is passed unvalidated to charge() at line 16), and any authenticated caller can send it. Whether this is exploitable depends on whether req.payments.charge treats NaN as 0 or rejects it, and that code is not in the repo (cart.js is the only file), so impact cannot be decided.

verdict_facts.guard_found: Only Math.max(1, Math.floor(i.qty)) at cart.js:14, which doesn't stop NaN or Infinity. There is no array/shape check, no Number.isFinite check, no qty cap, and no total > 0 check. No auth restriction beyond the upstream-populated req.user.
verdict_facts.reason: At cart.js:14 `p * Math.max(1, Math.floor(i.qty))` yields NaN for a non-numeric qty, or for an unknown sku (undefined price at line 13), and the same applies to 1e999 (Infinity); the unvalidated total goes straight to `req.payments.charge` at cart.js:16 with no finite/positive check. Any authenticated user can do this, and what charge() does with NaN is not visible, so the severity depends on it.
